jobs.excerpt: • Location: Remote — U. S. -based required.  For this opening we give preference to candidates based in the Central or Mountain time zones; all zones are considered if the coverage window below genuinely works for your life.
jobs.description:
• Location: Remote — U.S.-based required. For this opening we give preference to candidates based in the Central or Mountain time zones; all zones are considered if the coverage window below genuinely works for your life.

  • Reports to: Head of Sales

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change (B4C) is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education programs — anchored by our Master's of Education — equip educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. We envision a world where school is about what truly matters: empowering students AND teachers to live purposeful, creative lives full of vitality, wholeness, and connection.

The role

You'll be a full-cycle inside sales professional guiding teachers through the decision to enroll in B4C's degree programs. Marketing fills your calendar with booked 1:1 phone calls — you run a consultative discovery conversation, help each educator reach an honest fit decision, and enroll the ones the program genuinely serves.

Know what you'd be selling: a Master's degree our graduates consistently describe as transformative — for their teaching, their wellbeing, and their lives. Every enrollment you close is a teacher who stays in the profession stronger than they came to it. Most sales jobs ask you to believe in the product as a professional courtesy; this one earns it.

Three things to know about how we work, because they tell you whether this seat is for you:

You'd be joining an awesome team

This is a small group of mission-driven professionals who genuinely like each other and are unusually good at what they do. We chase a team goal — the number belongs to all of us, not to a leaderboard of individuals — so the incentive is to make the person next to you better. Reps trade what's working in real time, review each other's calls in the film room, and celebrate each other's wins loudly. If you've worked somewhere the top closer hoarded their tricks and the floor went quiet when someone was behind, this will feel different on day one.

We take selling seriously as a craft

Our motion is documented and built from what our best people actually do, not from theory — most of our wins close on the first substantive conversation, carried by disciplined follow-up. Everything we've built around it — the playbook, the coaching, the AI tooling — exists to get you to full speed fast: weeks, not quarters. After that, the book is yours to run. There are no individual volume quotas and no commission — we make sure you have a strong, steady set of calls, flexing up and down a bit during the highest-demand weeks and months, but overall protecting your calendar against getting overloaded. We hire people who run their own week, and then we get out of the way.

We sell with integrity, structurally

Teachers are trust professionals and our buyers for life — pressure tactics, false urgency, and manufactured scarcity don't just violate our values, they're incompatible with how we're regulated and how we retain students. Honest disqualification is a celebrated outcome. The product is what makes this possible: our graduates rate the program at an NPS in the +70s, so the honest conversation and the effective one are the same conversation. If your best work happens when you're allowed to tell a prospect the truth, you'll like it here.

What you'll actually do

  • Run ~8–12 scheduled discovery calls a day* (20 minutes each) with teachers who booked time to talk about the M.Ed. — assess fit, run real discovery, answer program and financing questions, and ask for the enrollment decision when the signal is there. *Daily volume fluctuates with seasonality, events, and experience.

  • Own the follow-up between calls: short, purposeful texting that protects shows and carries momentum, completion calls that finish decisions, and the follow-through that means nothing you promised a teacher ever slips.

  • Sell when teachers can talk. During the school year our calls concentrate in two windows: teachers' planning/lunch periods (roughly noon–2pm ET) and after school (roughly 4–8pm ET); in summer the weight shifts earlier. Your core coverage window is approximately noon–8pm ET on weekdays — in Central or Mountain time that's an ordinary late-morning-to-early-evening day, which is why we prefer those zones. Our best reps design their week around the teacher's clock on purpose; this role requires that design to be genuine and sustainable, not overtime.

  • Hand each newly enrolled educator cleanly to our onboarding team. Your job is the decision — a dedicated team carries students from deposit to day one, so your selling time stays selling time.

  • Bring what you learn back to the team: film-room participation, script feedback, sharing what's working. Our playbook carries our reps' wording because their wording works.

Who we're looking for

  • A proven consultative closer. 2+ years in a full-cycle closing role — high-consideration B2C (education, financial services, insurance, home services, coaching/wellness programs) or similar consultative sales — with a track record you can quantify and explain how it was measured.

  • One-conversation instincts. You know how to earn a decision in the first call when the fit is real — discovery first, then a direct, unapologetic ask — and how to walk away warmly when it isn't.

  • Follow-through as craft. You can describe the actual system you use to keep 100+ open conversations from slipping. Organized is table stakes; we're looking for someone who treats follow-up as the job, not the interruption.

  • A fast, eager tool adopter. This role runs on systems — a CRM (HubSpot a plus), AI-assisted call review and coaching, texting and scheduling tools, Google Workspace — and the stack keeps getting better. You don't just tolerate new tools; you pick them up quickly, fold them into how you work, and treat them as part of the craft.

  • A calendar owner. You manage your own energy and hours like a professional athlete — boundaries, blocks, evening selling by design, recovery budgeted after surges.

  • A teammate on purpose. Our reps get better in public — film-room reviews, script feedback, lending your wording to the playbook when it works. You want colleagues who sharpen your game and you return the favor; closers who guard their tricks don't thrive here.

  • Mission-resonant. You care that the thing you're selling genuinely changes teachers' lives, and you can say why in your own words. Our best closers are here on purpose — selling work that matters is the point.

You do NOT need admissions, higher-ed, or education-industry experience. We'll teach you the domain, the program, and the playbook — that's what our onboarding and coaching system is for. What we can't teach in eight weeks is professional selling. If you're a great closer who has always wanted your work to mean something, this is the seat.

Growth

This role has a real career ladder: EDC → Senior EDC, with promotion earned on craft, ownership, team impact, and judgment — assessed from your actual work, not tenure. Our most recent Senior promotion went to a rep whose calls became the film-room examples the team learns from. We promote from within on purpose.

Why this seat

Sales careers rarely offer all three: a product with real outcomes, a team of mission-driven professionals who treat selling as a craft worth studying and pull for each other, and a mission you'd defend at dinner. Teachers are holding up the hardest job in America, and the ones who find us are looking for a way to grow without leaving the classroom. You'd be the person who helps them decide well. If you've been waiting for a reason to bring your best selling somewhere it counts, this is it.

Compensation & benefits

  • Base salary: $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience and demonstrated track record

  • Equity eligibility (varies by experience)

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401k and FSA/HSA eligibility

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Note: per our accreditation and Title IV compliance posture, compensation is never linked to enrollment counts — raises and promotions are earned on craft and professional factors. (Stated here because good salespeople always ask.)

How to apply

The application asks five short questions — they matter more than your résumé, and we read every answer.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $80K - $100K

We are looking for a Senior Lead - Shared Services to join our Human Resources group; as we scale up and drive digital and financial inclusion across our markets.

Job Purpose

The Senior Lead – HR Shared Services is responsible for overseeing the delivery of efficient, accurate, and compliant HR operational services across the employee lifecycle. The role supports global and market-level HR operations, including employee records management, contracts administration, payroll input coordination, offboarding, and employee relations case administration.

The position drives operational excellence through strong service governance, stakeholder management, risk controls, and continuous process improvement while ensuring consistent delivery against agreed service standards and SLAs.

Key Responsibilities

1. Service Delivery Leadership & Governance

  • Oversee day-to-day HR Shared Services operations, ensuring timely and accurate execution of activities across the employee lifecycle.

  • Coordinate workload allocation, prioritisation, and operational follow-through across the function.

  • Establish and maintain operational routines, service standards, and process handoffs.

  • Track and report service KPIs including SLA adherence, turnaround times, quality metrics, backlog management, and error rates.

  • Manage escalations, resolve operational bottlenecks, and ensure timely communication and case closure.

2. Stakeholder Management & Cross-functional Coordination

  • Partner with People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and HRIS teams to deliver seamless HR operational support.

  • Align stakeholders on timelines, approvals, documentation standards, and service expectations.

  • Translate policy or business changes into operational processes, templates, communications, and training materials.

  • Provide operational updates, risk reporting, and improvement recommendations to People leadership where required.

3. Records & Data Governance

  • Ensure employee records and documentation are complete, accurate, and compliant with internal and regulatory requirements.

  • Conduct regular audits to identify and resolve data inconsistencies or compliance gaps.

  • Maintain confidentiality and strong controls around employee data handling and storage.

  • Drive HR data quality initiatives and implement preventive controls to minimise recurring errors.

4. Contracts & Employment Lifecycle Administration

  • Oversee employment contract issuance, renewals, amendments, and extensions within established timelines.

  • Ensure all employee documentation is accurately maintained within HR systems and document repositories.

  • Manage probation administration processes including confirmations, extensions, and related approvals.

  • Support performance management cycle administration, including documentation, letters, approvals tracking, and records management.

  • Ensure compliance with approval workflows, documentation standards, and record retention requirements.

5. Payroll Input Coordination

  • Coordinate monthly payroll input readiness by managing timelines, approvals, and submission requirements.

  • Oversee preparation and validation of payroll-related inputs, including commissions, bonuses, and employee lifecycle changes.

6. Offboarding Operations

  • Manage escalations and exceptions to minimise operational risk and maintain a positive employee experience.

7. Employee Relations Case Administration

  • Maintain secure and confidential employee relations records in line with company policies and compliance requirements.

  • Support maintenance of ER templates, SOPs, and operational guidance documentation.

  • Coordinate timely follow-up and closure of employee relations cases.

8. Continuous Improvement & Operational Controls

  • Identify operational inefficiencies and implement practical process improvements, templates, and standardisation initiatives.

  • Support process mapping, SOP documentation, and operational training activities.

  • Strengthen operational controls relating to approvals, documentation, segregation of duties, and audit readiness.

  • Drive adoption of process enhancements and ensure operational consistency across the function.

9. Data Analytics, Reporting & AI Enablement

  • Analyse operational service data to identify trends, bottlenecks, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Develop and maintain dashboards covering SLA performance, service quality, payroll exceptions, and case management metrics.

  • Partner with HRIS and People Systems teams to support automation and AI-enabled HR operations initiatives.

  • Ensure AI-enabled processes comply with data privacy, governance, and documentation standards.

  • Use operational insights to support decision-making and improve employee experience outcomes.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

Professional Certification

  • Certified HR Practitioner in Ghana, preferably CIHRM

Experience

  • 4–5 years’ experience in HR Shared Services, HR Operations, or employee lifecycle administration roles.

  • Hands-on experience across HR records management, contracts administration, payroll coordination, offboarding, and employee relations support.

About the Role

This role sits at the intersection of robotics and data infrastructure at a well-funded, early-stage robotics company. You'll be responsible for building reliable pipelines and storage systems that make large volumes of robot telemetry and sensor data usable for engineering and ML teams. Your work will directly enable faster iteration and safer robotic systems — from raw sensor ingestion all the way through to training-ready datasets and real-time analytics.

You'll join a cross-functional team of robotics engineers, software engineers, and data scientists in a fast-paced, on-site environment in Los Angeles, CA. This is a high-impact, hands-on role with broad scope at a company building at the frontier of physical AI and robotics.

Please note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build scalable data pipelines to ingest and process robot telemetry and sensor data (camera, LiDAR, IMU, and more).

  • Implement storage solutions and schemas that support analytics, model training, and data replay.

  • Ensure data quality, validation, and lineage across ingestion and transformation stages.

  • Optimize latency and throughput for both real-time and batch processing use cases.

  • Instrument observability, monitoring, and alerting for data flows and infrastructure.

  • Collaborate closely with robotics engineers and data scientists to translate platform needs into production-grade implementations.

  • Productionize ETL/ELT workflows with CI/CD and automated testing.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve production incidents affecting data availability or correctness.

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience building data infrastructure or engineering pipelines specifically for robotics sensor data — this is a dealbreaker requirement.

  • Proven experience designing, building, and maintaining data ingestion, processing, and storage pipelines for sensor data (e.g., camera, LiDAR, IMU).

  • Strong fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, and data pipeline design.

  • Proficiency in Python and/or C++ for building data tooling and pipelines.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud data platforms and distributed processing tools — e.g., AWS or GCP, Kafka or Pub/Sub, Spark or Flink, Airflow.

  • Experience with containerization and deployment of data pipelines using Docker and Kubernetes, plus basic CI/CD.

  • Experience with time-series databases and telemetry data management in a robotics context.

  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset for working across engineering and ML teams.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with ROS / ROS2 robotics middleware.

  • Familiarity with ML workflow tooling such as MLFlow or Kubeflow for end-to-end robotics data pipelines.

  • Experience with robotics simulation tools (e.g., Gazebo) and synthetic data generation.

  • Prior experience in an early-stage or high-growth startup environment.

Location

This is a full-time, on-site role based in Los Angeles, CA. Candidates based in or willing to relocate to the Los Angeles area are strongly preferred. The company also has a presence in New York City, NY and San Francisco, CA.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation will be competitive and commensurate with experience, including equity participation appropriate for an early-stage company. Specific details will be shared during the interview process.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. The system must handle multi-step reasoning, interact with external tools, and remain reliable despite non-deterministic model behavior. Our objective is to help users complete tasks daily enjoyable with over ~90%* reduced time.

Role

As Technical Lead, Machine Learning, you own the execution layer of A1’s intelligence. You translate research direction into reliable, scalable, production-grade ML systems.

This role sits at the intersection of research, infrastructure, and product. You are responsible for making models trainable, deployable, observable, and performant under real-world constraints.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end ML system execution: data pipelines, training workflows, evaluation systems, inference architecture, and deployment.

  • Fine-tune and adapt models using state-of-the-art methods such as LoRA, QLoRA, SFT, DPO, and distillation.

  • Architect and operate scalable inference systems, balancing latency, cost, and reliability.

  • Design and maintain data systems for high-quality synthetic and real-world training data.

  • Implement evaluation pipelines covering performance, robustness, safety, and bias, in partnership with research leadership.

  • Own production deployment, including GPU optimization, memory efficiency, latency reduction, and scaling policies.

  • Collaborate closely with application engineering to integrate ML systems cleanly into backend, mobile, and desktop products.

  • Make pragmatic trade-offs and ship improvements quickly, learning from real usage.

  • Work under real production constraints: latency, cost, reliability, and safety

Outcomes

  • Research and models reliably translate into production-ready solutions with clear performance and quality targets.

  • ML pipelines, training loops, and inference systems are stable, efficient, and maintainable.

  • Production issues are detected, debugged, and resolved quickly, minimizing user impact.

  • Team members are supported, aligned, and able to deliver high-impact ML work with minimal friction.

  • Iterations on models and systems are measurable, safe, and improve user experience over time.

Tech Stack

  • Python

  • PyTorch / JAX

  • GPU-based training and inference system

Ideal Experience

  • You have built or shipped real ML systems used by people, not just demos.

  • You are comfortable working with large models and understanding their failure modes.

  • You write strong, production-grade code and care about system correctness.

  • You are self-directed, pragmatic, and take full ownership of outcomes.

  • You communicate clearly and collaborate well in small, high-trust teams.

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

Role Summary

The Risk team at Imprint is responsible for making smarter, faster credit decisions that balance growth with responsible risk management. The team builds the models, policies, and analytical systems that power underwriting, fraud detection, and portfolio optimization across all of Imprint’s credit programs.

As a Data Scientist, Risk, you will own the modeling powering Imprint’s top-of-funnel credit decisioning—from application intake through approval—across every acquisition channel: direct affiliates (Credit Karma, NerdWallet), invitation-to-apply emails, direct mail, paid social, instant prescreens, and on-site applications. Your primary focus will be improving approval rates while maintaining credit quality: building better underwriting models, designing policy experiments, and uncovering segments where we can safely expand access to credit.

This role sits at the intersection of credit and acquisition strategy. You will partner directly with Credit Strategy, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to build targeting models for new channels, evaluate channel-level credit performance, and connect acquisition volume to downstream economics—approval rates, vintage loss forecasts, LTV, CAC, and contribution profit. Increasingly, that means building not just analyses but AI-powered systems that can autonomously monitor approval rate, channel performance, diagnose shifts, and recommend policy adjustments.

The Opportunity

  • Own and improve the full top-of-funnel credit decisioning pipeline: application scoring, policy rules, decline waterfalls, and approval rate optimization across direct affiliates, invitation-to-apply, direct mail, paid social, instant prescreens, and on-site applications

  • Build and iterate on underwriting, targeting, and segmentation models that expand safe approvals and improve channel-level acquisition quality

  • Design and analyze A/B tests and champion/challenger experiments on credit policies, establishing a test-and-learn cadence with structured readouts on both acquisition and credit performance

  • Build channel-level performance models that connect application volume to downstream economics: approval rates, expected losses, LTV, CAC, and contribution profit

  • Design and build agentic workflows and AI-powered monitoring systems that autonomously detect approval rate anomalies, diagnose score drift and population mix changes, and recommend policy adjustments

  • Partner directly with Credit Strategy, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to develop targeting criteria and risk frameworks for new and emerging acquisition channels

  • Build segmentation frameworks to identify underserved populations where credit access can be responsibly expanded

Your Profile

Required

  • 5 to 8+ years of experience in data science, risk analytics, or a related quantitative field, ideally at a high-growth startup or fintech company

  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with the ability to build models, transform raw data, and create custom datasets from complex financial data

  • Experience building credit risk or targeting models (scorecards, underwriting models, segmentation) or similar predictive modeling in a regulated environment

  • Deep understanding of statistical inference, experimentation design, and causal analysis, with the ability to disentangle policy impact from population shifts and channel mix changes

  • Comfort with AI tools and AI-native workflows; you actively use tools like Claude, Copilot, or similar to accelerate your work and are excited to build AI-powered analytical systems

  • Full-stack problem-solving orientation: you dive into messy data, trace a decline to its root cause, and question assumptions in pursuit of a better answer

  • Ability to present complex findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership and external partner stakeholders

  • Comfort owning projects end-to-end in a fast-moving startup environment with limited scaffolding, collaborating cross-functionally with Policy, Strategy, Product, and Engineering

Nice to Have

  • Experience with credit card underwriting, lending, or consumer credit products

  • Familiarity with credit bureau data (Vantage, FICO, tradeline attributes) and alternative data sources

  • Experience building or scaling experimentation infrastructure for credit policy testing

  • Exposure to fraud detection, KYC/IDV workflows, or application fraud models

  • Understanding of acquisition channel economics and experience partnering with marketing or credit strategy teams on targeting and LTV modeling

We don't expect every candidate to check every box. If this role excites you and you bring strong fundamentals, we encourage you to apply.

Stack

Python and SQL for modeling and analysis. Snowflake for data warehousing. AWS infrastructure. Dashboarding and monitoring tools for production systems.

Learn More

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

About the Role

A small, fast-moving defense tech startup in Austin, TX is hiring a hands-on Senior Robotics Engineer to design the physical control systems powering high-speed interceptor platforms. This is an onsite, mission-critical role sitting at the intersection of control theory, embedded software, and real-world robotics — directly impacting system performance against emerging threats. You'll be a core member of a tight-knit engineering team focused on shipping field-ready capability.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement physical control systems — the "body" — for interceptor platforms.

  • Develop high-bandwidth control loops and advanced control algorithms (e.g., PID, model-predictive, adaptive control) to ensure vehicle stability and precise high-speed maneuvers under dynamic load.

  • Write high-quality, efficient embedded code (primarily Rust, C, or C++) to manage actuators, motor drivers (via CAN bus), and sensors on RTOS.

  • Integrate and fuse camera and IMU data (e.g., EKF/UKF) on embedded platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson for reliable, real-time state estimation.

  • Translate computer-vision tracking output into reliable motor commands that steer the interceptor.

  • Build and maintain Python-based tools for calibration, logging, and CI/CD to support rapid iteration and deployment.

  • Work fully onsite in Austin, TX as a full-time member of a small, senior engineering team.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 6+ years of relevant experience in robotics, controls, or embedded systems.

  • Strong control theory fundamentals — expertise in PID, model-predictive or adaptive control, and performance tuning for robotics.

  • Proficiency in Rust, C, or C++ for embedded, low-latency hardware interaction.

  • Deep experience with embedded platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson), camera pipelines, IMUs, and sensor fusion techniques (EKF/UKF).

  • Hands-on knowledge of motor drivers, CAN bus, RTOS, and ROS2/DDS or similar middleware.

  • End-to-end autonomy development experience: translating computer vision outputs into reliable motor commands.

  • U.S. citizenship and ability to pass a background check; existing security clearance or ability to obtain one is required.

  • A demonstrated passion for building robots or engineering projects — in or out of work.

Nice to Have

  • PCB design familiarity and EMC awareness; experience with oscilloscopes, logic/CAN analyzers, and basic rework.

  • Prior defense startup or mission-driven product experience.

  • Safety-critical workflow experience.

  • Model-predictive or adaptive control expertise beyond PID.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $150,000 – $250,000 USD annually, commensurate with experience.

  • Equity participation in an early-stage, high-growth defense tech company.

  • Comprehensive benefits package.

Location

This role is fully onsite in Austin, TX. Remote and hybrid arrangements are not available. Visa sponsorship is not available — U.S. citizenship is required for security clearance eligibility.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Analyst
jobs.excerpt: Strategic Finance Analyst | M-KOPA You've built three-statement models under deadline pressure for deals that closed, got filed, and were forgotten within a quarter.
jobs.description:
Strategic Finance Analyst | M-KOPA

You've built three-statement models under deadline pressure for deals that closed, got filed, and were forgotten within a quarter. What if the next model you build determined how a company gets 3 million more customers access to credit for the first time?

That's the actual trade-off on the table here.

M-KOPA has just crossed 7 million customers across Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, and South Africa, with more than $2 billion in credit unlocked. Of those customers, 55% are accessing formal financial services for the first time, and 86% report a real improvement in their quality of life. We're not a mature business optimising at the margins — we're building the financial infrastructure for the next stage of that growth, from 5 million customers to 7 million, and now toward 10 million.

Why this role exists right now

Every one of those growth milestones has to be modelled, stress-tested, and defended before it becomes a board decision. That's the job of the Strategic Finance team — we own the Long-Range Plan, the market entry business cases, and the analysis that sits behind what the CEO, COO, and board actually decide to do next. As the business scales into new markets and new products, that modelling work is only getting more complex, and more visible. We need someone whose technical rigour can anchor it.

What makes this different from a typical FP&A or banking analyst seat

Most modelling roles either sit inside a bank, building work that ends at deal close, or inside a corporate finance function, running templates someone else designed years ago. This one is neither. You'll be building models from a blank sheet — for market entry decisions, unit economics, distribution cost structures, and funding scenarios — and you'll be doing it in direct partnership with the Head of Strategic Finance, on workstreams that land in front of the CEO and the board within weeks, not quarters. You stay as technical as you were in banking. You just get to see what your numbers actually build.

What you'd own

The core of the role is the company's Long-Range Plan — base, stretch, and market-specific upside/downside scenarios, with the assumptions packs and documentation that leadership and the board rely on. Beyond that, you'll build audit-ready models for special projects as they come up: a new market entry case one month, a distribution cost model the next, a funding analysis after that. You'll be the person who catches the balance sheet or cash flow tie-out break before it reaches the CEO's desk, not after. And you'll support the monthly and quarterly FP&A cycle — budget-vs-actual variance, performance commentary, reporting packs — while helping migrate planning processes into Anaplan as the team scales its tooling across markets.

A good amount of this role is architecture before arithmetic: taking a half-specified problem and figuring out the right model structure before you touch a single formula.

What you'd bring

  • Demonstrable experience building complex, three-statement models from scratch under deadline pressure, ideally from an investment banking, transaction services, or similarly rigorous modelling background

  • A genuine fluency in how operational drivers flow through to financial statements — you don't just build the model, you understand why each line moves the way it does

  • Relentless attention to detail paired with the communication skill to defend your assumptions and explain your logic to someone who's never opened the model

It also helps — though isn't required — if you've worked with Anaplan or another planning platform, have exposure to fintech, lending, or consumer credit, or have worked across multi-currency, multi-entity African businesses.

The honest version

This role moves between workstreams — the Long-Range Plan one week, an ECL question the next, a market entry case after that — often with incomplete information and a deadline that doesn't move. You'll need to get productive on unfamiliar terrain fast, more than once. If that sounds exhausting rather than energising, this probably isn't your seat. If it sounds like exactly the kind of variety your current role doesn't give you, it might be.

Why it's worth the trade-off

You stay deeply technical. Your analysis directly shapes what a high-growth company does next, with executive visibility from day one, and a clear line into senior strategic finance leadership as the team and the business scale together.

If you're reading this and already thinking about how you'd structure the model — that's probably the signal. Let's talk.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at .

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships.

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.

Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references.

Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Director of Developer Experience, you will be tasked with leading the organization responsible for how every engineer at the company builds, tests, ships, and operates software. You will own two interconnected functions: Infrastructure Services (CI/CD orchestration, GitOps continuous delivery, artifact management, and related platforms) and Developer Tooling (the teams that design and operate our CI/CD pipelines and internal developer platform). Critically, you will also define and execute our strategy for integrating AI across the software development lifecycle, from AI-assisted code generation and review to AI-driven engineering intelligence platforms.

Developer experience is one of the highest-leverage investments an engineering organization can make, and AI is the largest shift in how software is built in a generation. The Director of Developer Experience will directly shape how hundreds of engineers spend their day, how quickly we ship, how confidently we operate in production, and how effectively we harness AI across the SDLC. This is a critically important role with executive visibility and a clear mandate to deliver measurable results.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Lead, grow, and develop a multi-team organization of managers and senior engineers spanning Infrastructure Services and Developer Tooling.
  • Define and execute the vision for developer experience, including build, test, deployment, artifact management, internal platform capabilities, and AI-augmented developer workflows.
  • Own the strategy and rollout of AI tooling across the SDLC, including AI coding assistants, AI code review and PR automation, AI-assisted test generation, and AI engineering intelligence platforms. Drive adoption, measure impact, and ensure these tools are deployed safely and effectively.
  • Ensure the availability, performance, and security of the systems that engineers depend on every day.
  • Drive the evolution of CI/CD pipelines to be faster, more reliable, more self-service, and more secure, including embedding AI capabilities such as automated triage, intelligent test selection, and AI-assisted incident response.
  • Establish metrics and use them to drive measurable improvement in developer productivity.
  • Partner with security, legal, and AI leadership to set policy for AI-generated code, IP and licensing, data handling, model selection, and acceptable-use guardrails.
  • Partner with security, SRE, product engineering, architecture, and AI/ML teams to align on standards, golden paths, and shared platforms.
  • Own the budget, tooling investments, and vendor relationships for the developer experience portfolio, including AI tooling spend.
  • Recruit, mentor, and retain exceptional engineering leaders and individual contributors.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 10+ years of progressive engineering experience, including 5+ years of engineering management and at least 2+ years leading managers (managing managers).
  • Demonstrated track record in building and scaling developer experience, platform engineering, or DevOps organizations in a mid-to-large engineering org.
  • Deep, hands-on familiarity with the modern CI/CD and developer tooling stack: Jenkins, ArgoCD, Artifactory or equivalents.
  • Practical experience evaluating, rolling out, and measuring the impact of AI developer tooling.
  • A clear point of view on how AI changes the SDLC and how to capture that value without compromising on security, code quality, or developer trust.
  • Strong understanding of Kubernetes, GitOps, containerization, and cloud-native deployment patterns.
  • Experience in defining and operating internal developer platforms and golden paths.
  • Excellent strategic thinking paired with a willingness to go deep on technical decisions when needed.
  • Strong communication and executive presence; able to influence across engineering and partner with security, compliance, legal, and product leadership.
  • A demonstrated bias toward developer empathy, self-service, and reducing toil.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. jobs.excerpt: Finance Transformation Manager — M-KOPA You know the difference between a demo and a system that survives contact with a trial balance.
jobs.description:
Finance Transformation Manager — M-KOPA

You know the difference between a demo and a system that survives contact with a trial balance. That's rarer than you think.

Most people who can talk fluently about AI have never had to make it work inside a real close process, a real audit trail, a real Anaplan model that finance actually trusts. M-KOPA is looking for someone who has — or someone ready to prove they can.

Where this sits. M-KOPA is one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs, now serving 7 million customers across five markets and having unlocked over $2 billion in credit. Behind those numbers is a finance function running on Microsoft Dynamics and Anaplan, increasingly threaded through with Claude, and a leadership team that's decided this is the moment to stop treating AI as an experiment and start treating it as infrastructure.

Why now. We've grown from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we're building toward 10 million next. That growth doesn't just need more finance headcount — it needs a finance function that runs leaner and smarter than the one that got us here. 86% of our customers report improved quality of life, and 70% use our products to generate income; the systems behind those numbers need to scale without the manual reconciliation and reporting drag that usually comes with scale. This role exists because our leadership has committed to closing that gap now, not after it becomes a bottleneck.

What makes this different. Most "finance transformation" roles are really change-management roles wearing a technical label — you'll sit in workshops, write recommendations, and hand them to someone else to build. This one isn't that. You'll sit inside the finance team, find the friction yourself, and build the fix yourself: deepening our Claude–Dynamics integration, designing agents and workflows that actually replace manual reconciliation work, and owning the result end to end. It's a builder's mandate with a finance brief, not an IT ticket queue.

What you'll bring.

  • Demonstrable experience deploying Claude (or a comparable AI system) in a real business context — prompt design, workflow automation, API integration, and artefacts that actually run in production. This is the single most important thing we're looking for, and we'll ask you to show us something real you've built, ideally involving a Dynamics-style integration.

  • A technical foundation strong enough to read a data model and a trial balance in the same afternoon, paired with exceptional learning aptitude — the proven ability to apply AI and engineering thinking to genuinely complex financial and accounting scenarios.

  • Working knowledge of how audit actually works in practice: mining and structuring data for external and internal audit processes, and following through on remediation of findings, not just producing the report.

What the work looks like. Some weeks you're deep in the weeds of a Dynamics-Anaplan integration, chasing down why two systems disagree on a number. Other weeks you're building an agent that turns a two-day reconciliation into a two-hour one, then coaching the finance team on when to trust it and when not to. You'll be the person finance calls when something's slow, and the person engineering calls when they need someone who actually understands what a close process demands. Data integrity — one source of truth across the finance stack — sits with you.

Reality check. This role asks you to be genuinely bilingual between finance and engineering, and there's no playbook to hand you — you'll be writing it as you go, often while systems are live and numbers are due. If that sounds like friction rather than freedom, this probably isn't the role. If it sounds like exactly the kind of problem you've been waiting for someone to hand you, you're probably ready for it.

Where you work from. This role is remote or based in any of our operating markets — we're more interested in what you can build than where you build it from.

jobs.excerpt: About the CompanyAt Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business.
jobs.description:
About the Company

At Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business.A leader in autonomous driving since 2007, Torc has spent over a decade commercializing our solutions with experienced partners. Now a part of the Daimler family, we are focused solely on developing software for automated trucks to transform how the world moves freight.  Join us and catapult your career with the company that helped pioneer autonomous technology, and the first AV software company with the vision to partner directly with a truck manufacturer. 

Meet the Team

The Auto Tagger team is the engine behind our data flywheel, responsible for translating petabytes of raw, multi-modal vehicle data into a highly curated library of critical driving scenarios. By mining driving logs for long-tail events, we provide the foundational data required for safe autonomous trucking. Leveraging Pegasus logical layers, this team structures and catalogs findings into an observations database that directly accelerates development across autonomous perception, sensor fusion, and generative simulation testing.

What You'll Do

  • Integrate and deploy automated event-tagger into production pipelines, running and monitoring tagging tasks at scale across petabytes of vehicle log data.
  • Build and maintain the data engineering pipelines that organize, structure, and catalog tagged scenario data into the observations database.
  • Own CI/CD for the Auto Tagger pipeline using GitHub Actions, keeping deployments reliable, tested, and repeatable.
  • Write production grade code in Python across the pipeline, from data ingestion and transformation through model integration and deployment.
  • Build and operate on Databricks for large scale data processing, interactive querying, and pipeline orchestration.
  • Design, deploy, and scale AWS infrastructure (as code) to support high-volume, distributed processing of vehicle log pipelines — working with structured/tagged outputs and metadata.
  • Instrument pipelines with logging, metrics, and alerting; own on-call response for tagging job failures and data quality regressions.
  • Partner with ML engineers on the team to take tagging and classification models from development into a scalable, monitored production pipeline.
  • Ensure data quality and metadata integrity as tagged events move from raw logs into the observations database used by perception, simulation, and systems teams.
  • Troubleshoot and improve pipeline performance, reliability, and cost as data volume and model complexity grow.

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with 5+ years of software engineering experience, including production data pipeline or ML infrastructure work.
  • Strong Python skills, with experience building and maintaining production data or ML pipelines.
  • Hands-on CI/CD experience, GitHub Actions required.
  • Required experience with Databricks for large scale data processing and orchestration.
  • Required experience with AWS, including infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or CloudFormation) for provisioning distributed processing infrastructure.
  • Experience processing large scale time series or unstructured datasets.
  • Experience with observability tooling (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch) for production pipeline monitoring and alerting.
  • Experience integrating and deploying ML models into production systems — serving, monitoring, and rollback, not just training.
  • Strong communication skills to work across ML, perception, and simulation teams.

Bonus Points!

  • Familiarity with auto-labeling pipelines, VLMs, or zero-shot classification for scenario extraction.
  • Experience with distributed compute frameworks such as Ray, Spark, or Daft.
  • Familiarity with robotics data formats (ROS bags, MCAP) and columnar storage formats (Parquet, Arrow).
  • Experience with model serving frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang.
  • Familiarity with scenario description standards like Pegasus layers.

Perks of Being a Torc'r

Torc cares about our team members and we strive to provide benefits and resources to support their health, work/life balance, and future. Our culture is collaborative, energetic, and team focused. Torc offers:

  • A competitive compensation package that includes a bonus component and stock options
  • 100% paid medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees
  • 401K plan with a 6% employer match
  • Flexibility in schedule and generous paid vacation (available immediately after start date)
  • Company-wide holiday office closures
  • AD+D and Life Insurance

At Torc, we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We celebrate the uniqueness of our Torc'rs and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, veteran status, or disabilities. Even if you don't meet 100% of the qualifications listed for this opportunity, we encourage you to apply.

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several geographic markets. Pay is based on a number of factors and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Torc's total compensation package will also include our corporate bonus and stock option plan. Dependent on the position offered, sign-on payments, relocation, and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits.

About Matter Health

Matter Health delivers primary and preventive healthcare directly to older adults living in affordable housing communities. Our mission is simple: to improve healthcare access by meeting patients where they are and building trusted relationships within the communities we serve. As we rapidly expand across the country, we are building a team of mission-driven professionals who thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments.

Total Healthcare. Where you live.

About the Role

Matter Health is seeking a Senior Vice President, Clinical Quality & Population Health to lead the enterprise functions that drive clinical quality, population-health outcomes, value-based performance, and operational excellence across our patient populations.

Reporting to the Chief Medical Officer, this executive will lead a multidisciplinary team with accountability across Medicare Star Ratings and quality performance, clinical programs, clinical operations, coding and clinical documentation, risk adjustment, and provider credentialing.

This leader will serve as a dyad partner to the SVP of Operations, helping ensure that Matter Health’s clinical and operational strategies remain aligned and mutually reinforcing. The SVP will also serve as a key liaison to the Chief Medical Officer’s Clinical Affairs function and represent Quality and Clinical Programs in executive discussions, payer relationships, board reporting, and regulatory interactions.

This is both a strategic and execution-focused leadership position. The ideal candidate will bring deep experience in Medicare Star Ratings, HEDIS, CAHPS, value-based care, and enterprise clinical-quality leadership. jobs.description:
About the Team

HubSpot’s Downmarket Product Org is responsible for overseeing our broader portfolio of freemium products - shaping the core product experience and powering every key moment in the customer lifecycle, from the first interaction through long term retention and expansion.

We are scaling our Monetization function within this team. The group will focus on one of the most important and interesting challenges in software today: determining how to help customers discover and purchase your product in the age of AI and Agents, for headless and UI-based use cases, and with credits as an emerging pricing model.

About the Role

The traditional PLG monetization model was built for a world of static, tier-based upgrades accessed through a point-and-click UI. We are moving toward agent-based, credit-priced products distributed across multiple surfaces - including APIs and LLM interfaces - and our buying strategy must evolve to match.

As a Staff Product Manager for Monetization and Product Led Growth, you will own the evolution of this buying experience. This will include two charters:

  • Being the single person who can oversee the entire end-to-end buying journey across various prospect and customer touchpoints
  • Rebuilding our monetization infrastructure from static upgrade prompts in HubSpot’s UI, to agentically delivered, just-in-time, contextual upgrade moments delivered both in-app and via LLM interfaces. We will define and build the capabilities to recommend and sell the right product to the right customer at the right time, agnostic of whether they are using HubSpot in our app or via MCP.

What You Will Do

  • You will own the buying, product discovery, and upgrade experience across HubSpot. You will be the single Product Manager accountable for how customers move from our freemium funnel to the solutions that best meet their needs.
  • You will define HubSpot’s Product Led Monetization strategy for the AI era. This includes evolving from static upgrade triggers to personalized, context aware upgrade moments powered by large language models and delivered through conversational assistants and MCP. You will help define what an upgrade moment looks like and means when users don’t have a traditional UI to interact with and monetization becomes more usage-based.
  • You will partner with product teams across HubSpot to align buying patterns and create a coherent, consistent customer experience across the platform.
  • You will work closely with go to market teams on pricing launches, upgrade campaigns, and customer communication strategies related to driving monetization.
  • You will present strategies, progress, and results to senior leaders, including members of the executive team.

What We Are Looking For

  • You have owned monetization or the buying experience for a software as a service product. This is a core area of expertise for you.
  • You have worked on a product with credit based, usage based, or outcome based pricing. You understand how these models affect both how a product is built and how it is sold.
  • You have driven alignment across multiple product groups without relying on direct authority. You know how to influence decisions, build commitment, and move teams toward a shared outcome.
  • You have meaningful AI product experience. You have worked on or alongside products built around artificial intelligence, and you understand how large language models are changing product strategy, customer expectations, and business models.
  • You bring strong business model fluency. You can think strategically about pricing, packaging, monetization, and go to market motions, not only feature roadmaps.
  • You have worked in both a scaled organization and a more entrepreneurial environment. You can navigate the complexity of a large company while remaining comfortable building something new from the ground up.
  • You are a driver who moves quickly and takes ownership. You are comfortable challenging existing approaches when needed, and you do not wait for perfect information before making progress.

Why This Role Matters

The entire software industry is working to determine how AI products should be priced, packaged, and sold.

HubSpot has more than 250,000 customers, an active credit based monetization system, strong Agents and usage through MCPs. In this role, you will be at the center of translating those strengths into the next generation of Product Led Growth, not as a theoretical exercise, but through products and experiences used by real customers.

This is a Staff level opportunity with meaningful greenfield scope, direct visibility with executive leadership, and the chance to define what Product Led Growth looks like at one of the most recognized brands in software as a service.

In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

Trans Lifeline is a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing our trans peers with the connection, care, and advocacy we need and deserve. Founded in 2014, Trans Lifeline operates three core program areas that serve the trans and gender-nonconforming (GNC) community:

  1. Our Hotline program, which operates a confidential peer-support hotline for trans and (GNC) folks, staffed by trans and GNC folks, where we provide emotional support, crisis intervention, and referrals to resources such as healthcare, housing, and legal assistance.

We’re expanding across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, and Peru, and we’re looking for an experienced Clinical Data Manager to help build the foundation of our growing LATAM Data Management team, ensuring the delivery of high-quality clinical data that drives successful clinical trials and accelerates innovative therapies to patients.

The Senior Clinical Data Manager/Principal Clinical Data Manager is responsible and manages all aspects of the clinical trial data management process from study start up to post database lock for assigned projects. Standard Operating Procedures / Work Instructions (SOPs/WIs); regulatory directives; study specific plans and guidelines will be followed. This position will also oversee and/or perform database development and testing.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

  • Primary Data Management (DM) contact (Lead DM role) for assigned clinical project(s) / program(s), ensuring that there is back-up, continuity, responsiveness, and that tasks are performed in a timely manner. May support another Lead DM as a back-up and/or team member. May include DM oversight of sponsor programs.
  • Oversee project data entry process including development of data entry guidelines, training, data entry quality and resourcing
  • May perform quality control of data entry
  • Provide input, assesses and manage timelines. Ensure that clinical data management deadlines are met with quality. Assess resource needs for assigned projects, as needed.
  • Develop CRF specifications from the clinical study protocol and coordinate the review/feedback from all stakeholders
  • May assist in building clinical databases
  • Conduct database build UAT and maintain quality controlled database build documentation. Oversee overall quality of the clinical database.
  • May specify requirements for all edit check types e.g. electronic, manual data review, edit checks, etc. Oversee development of the edit check specifications and manual data review specifications
  • Responsible for creating, revising, appropriate versioning and maintaining data management documentation. Oversee completeness of data management documentation for the Trial Master File.
  • Train clinical research personnel on the study specific CRF, EDC, and other project related items as needed.
  • Review and query clinical trial data according to the Data Management Plan
  • Perform line listing data review based on the guidance provided by the sponsor and/or Lead DM
  • Run patient and study level status and metric reporting
  • Perform medical coding of medical terms relative to each other in order to ensure medical logic and consistency
  • Coordinate SAE/AE reconciliation
  • Liaises with third-party vendors such as external data and EDC vendors in a project-manager capacity in support of timelines and data-related deliverables
  • May assist with SAS programming and quality control of SAS programs used in the Data Management department
  • Identify and troubleshoot operational problems, issues, obstacles, and barriers for studies based on metrics data, audit reports, and input from project team members and other stakeholders
  • May assist in reviewing and providing feedback on protocols, Statistical Analysis Plans (SAP) and Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), if required by the project
  • Participate in the development and maintenance of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and corresponding process documentation related to data management and database management activities
  • May attend strategy meetings, bid defense prep meetings, bid defenses, capability presentations, potential client engagement meetings
  • May review Request for Proposals (RFP), proposals, provide project estimates
  • Provide leadership for cross-functional and organization-wide initiatives, where applicable
  • Trains and ensures that all data management project team members have been sufficiently trained
  • Communicate with study sponsors, vendors and project teams as needed regarding data, database or other relevant project issues
  • May present software demonstrations/trainings, department/company training sessions, present at project meetings
  • May require some travel
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:
Minimum Required:

  • Bachelors and/or a combination of related experience

Other Required:

  • 8+ years’ experience for a Sr. Clinical Data Manager and 10+ years for a Principal Clinical Data Manager
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook
  • Able to handle a variety of clinical research tasks
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills
  • Professional use of the English language; both written and oral
  • Experience in utilizing various clinical database management systems
  • Broad knowledge of drug, device and/or biologic development and effective data management practices
  • Strong representational skills, ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing
  • Strong leadership and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to undertake occasional travel

Preferred:

  • Experience in a clinical, scientific or healthcare discipline
  • Dictionary medical coding (MedDRA and WHODrug)
  • Understanding of CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM, ADaM, etc.…)
  • Oncology and/or Orphan Drug therapeutic experience

jobs.title: Head of Quality Engineering (Remote - Work from Anywhere)
jobs.excerpt: Work from anywhere, impact everywhere Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
jobs.description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position

Work from anywhere!

Position overview

We're looking for a Head of Quality Engineering to join our technology function, reporting directly to the CTO. At Xapo, we are building truly cross-functional teams with full ownership of design, architecture, building, testing, delivery, data, and operations, structured as Stream Aligned Teams (SATs), Platform teams and Enabling teams as per Team Topologies.

This role owns the quality framework across the entire technology function, coverage standards, gate criteria, AI-assisted test tooling, SAT enablement, and pre-release veto authority. You give engineering, apps, and web a single accountable owner for what "quality" means and how it is measured.

This is not a traditional QA role. You will not sit in a test team checking other people's code, SAT engineers own quality in their own code (shift-left). You own the system engineers test within: the framework, the tooling, the gates, and the standards.

The role is deliberately tooling-heavy over headcount-heavy. Your budget is for tooling and AI tokens, not for building a QA team beneath you. The agentic QA pipeline is already in active PoC with positive early results; you will own scaling it to production. Your north star: fully automated quality enforcement, where releases are blocked automatically when rigorous checks fail, without needing human intervention. Target: more than 80% of release quality decisions made by automated tooling within 12 months of hire.

This is an opportunity to shape how a regulated crypto bank defines and enforces software quality, at the intersection of engineering excellence, AI-assisted tooling, and a genuinely high-stakes production environment.

Responsibilities

  • Quality framework definition: own coverage standards (unit, service, integration, end-to-end), gate criteria, and the quality contribution to the function-level Definition of Done. Aligned with Head of Engineering on backend and Head of Frontend Engineering on client-side.
  • Coverage baselines: define measurable coverage thresholds per service and per tribe, with trend visibility, and drive adoption across teams.
  • Pre-release veto authority: hold and exercise the authority to block releases when quality gates are not met. Own the automated tooling that makes this veto self-triggering rather than dependent on a single person.
  • AI-assisted test tooling: define and drive the framework for automated test generation, regression coverage, integration test tooling, and the agentic QA pipeline. You are the designer and driver; implementation is a cross-functional effort with Platform, backend, web, and mobile engineers.
  • SAT enablement: produce the training, documentation, tooling, and templates that let Stream Aligned Team engineers do quality work themselves, without a separate QA function.
  • Test environment strategy: partner with Head of Platform Engineering on dedicated QA environments, test data management, and integration test infrastructure.
  • Quality posture reporting: own the metrics like defect escape rate, coverage trends, release veto rate, AI tooling adoption progress, and percentage of releases requiring no manual quality intervention.
  • Security testing integration: partner with Security on SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning as components of the quality gate.

Skills needed

  • 8+ years in software quality engineering, with a clear track record of owning quality frameworks across engineering organisations, not just managing a QA team or running manual test cycles.
  • Hands-on experience building CI/CD quality gates at multiple levels: unit, service, integration, and end-to-end. You know where tests go in a pipeline and how to make them block a release reliably.
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted test tooling, LLM-driven test generation, agentic QA pipelines, or equivalent. You don't need to have shipped a production-grade system, but you need a genuine point of view and hands-on exposure.
  • Demonstrated ability to raise quality standards without a reporting hierarchy, you have influenced engineering teams through better tooling, documentation, and frameworks, not through authority over people.
  • Solid understanding of distributed, event-driven microservices architectures and what testing them well requires: contract testing, consumer-driven contracts, integration test data strategies.
  • Experience defining and tracking quality metrics: defect escape rate, coverage baselines, release veto rates. You have turned quality into something measurable.
  • Strong written communication, you can write a coverage standard, gate criteria document, or enablement guide that engineers actually read and use.
  • Experience in regulated fintech, payments, or banking environments, with a strong emphasis on mobile-first product delivery. You have an appreciation for the stakes of a quality failure in a customer-funds context, particularly within the unique constraints and user expectations of a mobile application environment

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with agentic or generative AI test tooling in production or near-production contexts.
  • Familiarity with Team Topologies, how Stream Aligned, Platform, and Enabling teams interact in practice.
  • Security testing experience: SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, and how these integrate into a CI/CD quality gate.
  • Background in crypto, Web3, custody, or blockchain-based systems.
  • Open-source contributions or external thought leadership (talks, articles, OSS projects) related to quality engineering or test automation.

While your North Star is absolute automation, you possess a "roll-up-your-sleeves" mentality. You aren't afraid to get your hands dirty, jump into the trenches, and manually test the mobile apps yourself if a critical release or an edge-case roadblock requires it.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balanceBuild amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge.

  • Expect ExcellenceCollaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you’ll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.
